title: Kellerin alleviates cerebral ischemic injury by inhibiting ferroptosis via targeting Akt-mediated transcriptional activation of Nrf2.
authors: Mi, Yan; Wang, Yongping; Liu, Yeshu; Dang, Wen; Xu, Libin; Tan, Shaowen; Liu, Linge; Chen, Gang; Liu, Yueyang; Li, Ning; Hou, Yue
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 研究药物kellerin通过Akt/Nrf2通路抑制铁死亡减轻脑缺血损伤，虽涉及Nrf2转录激活但核心是药物-蛋白互作与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，仅分子对接为辅助手段，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) is characterized as a detrimental cerebrovascular disease with high mortality and disability. Ferroptosis is a novel mechanism involved in neuronal death. There is a close connection between IS and ferroptosis, and inhibiting ferroptosis may provide an effective strategy for treating IS. Our previous investigations have discovered that kellerin, the active compound of Ferula sinkiangensis K. M. Shen, possesses the capability to shield against cerebral ischemia injury. PURPOSE: Our objective is to clarify the relationship between the neuroprotective properties of kellerin against IS and its ability to modulate ferroptosis, and investigate the underlying regulatory pathway. STUDY DESIGN: We investigated the impact and mechanism of kellerin in C57BL/6 mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) as well as SH-SY5Y cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/ re-oxygenation (OGD/R). METHODS: The roles of kellerin on neurological severity, cerebral infarction and edema were investigated in vivo. The regulatory impacts of kellerin on ferroptosis, mitochondrial damage and Akt/Nrf2 pathway were explored. Molecular docking combined with drug affinity responsive target stability assay (DARTS) and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were performed to analyze the potential target proteins for kellerin. RESULTS: Kellerin protected against IS and inhibited ferroptosis in vivo. Meanwhile, kellerin improved the neuronal damage caused by OGD/R and suppressed ferroptosis by inhibiting the production of mitochondrial ROS in vitro. Further we found that kellerin directly interacted with Akt and enhanced its phosphorylation, leading to the increase of Nrf2 nuclear translocation and its downstream antioxidant genes expression. Moreover, kellerin's inhibitory effect on ferroptosis and mitochondrial ROS release was eliminated by inhibiting Akt/Nrf2 pathway. CONCLUSIONS: Our study firstly demonstrates that the neuroprotective properties of kellerin against IS are related to suppressing ferroptosis through inhibiting the production of mitochondrial ROS, in which its modulation on Akt-mediated transcriptional activation of Nrf2 plays an important role. This finding shed light on the potential mechanism that kellerin exerts therapeutic effects in IS.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血性卒中（Ischemic stroke, IS）是一种具有高死亡率和高致残率的有害脑血管疾病。铁死亡（ferroptosis）是参与神经元死亡的一种新机制。IS与铁死亡之间存在密切关联，抑制铁死亡可能为治疗IS提供有效策略。我们先前的研究发现，新疆阿魏（Ferula sinkiangensis K. M. Shen）的活性化合物kellerin具有保护脑缺血损伤的能力。目的：我们的目标是阐明kellerin对IS的神经保护特性与其调节铁死亡能力之间的关系，并探讨其潜在的调控通路。研究设计：我们研究了kellerin在经历大脑中动脉闭塞/再灌注（MCAO/R）的C57BL/6小鼠以及暴露于氧糖剥夺/再氧合（OGD/R）的SH-SY5Y细胞中的作用和机制。方法：在体内研究了kellerin对神经功能严重程度、脑梗死和水肿的作用。探讨了kellerin对铁死亡、线粒体损伤和Akt/Nrf2通路的调节影响。采用分子对接结合药物亲和响应靶标稳定性分析（DARTS）和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）来分析kellerin的潜在靶蛋白。结果：Kellerin在体内保护免受IS损伤并抑制铁死亡。同时，kellerin改善了OGD/R引起的神经元损伤，并通过抑制线粒体ROS的产生在体外抑制铁死亡。进一步我们发现，kellerin直接与Akt相互作用并增强其磷酸化，导致Nrf2核转位及其下游抗氧化基因表达增加。此外，kellerin对铁死亡和线粒体ROS释放的抑制作用通过抑制Akt/Nrf2通路而被消除。结论：我们的研究首次证明，kellerin对IS的神经保护特性与其通过抑制线粒体ROS产生来抑制铁死亡相关，其中其对Akt介导的Nrf2转录激活的调节起着重要作用。这一发现揭示了kellerin在IS中发挥治疗作用的潜在机制。
